intro: This is Maiden's Castle, in Mersin province, a sea castle of the 12th century rising from an islet two hundred metres offshore. It closed the harbour from one side, while Korykos Castle on the mainland closed the other: two guardians facing each other across the water.
history: The island castle was raised in the twelfth century under Byzantium. Later it passed to the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia, and then to the Karamanids. Between it and Korykos Castle on the shore, a chain could be drawn to close the harbour mouth. And the name? It comes from a tale: a king's daughter was shut up here to keep her from a prophesied snakebite.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the sea castle and Korykos Castle, and look out for the cisterns, the walls and the towers.
facts: Did you know? The water between the two castles is shallow, and in summer, swimmers making for the island are the most familiar sight of this coast. The castle covers the whole islet, two hundred metres offshore, holding one side of the harbour while Korykos Castle held the other. And its name comes from the story of a king's daughter, shut up here to keep her from a prophesied snakebite.
outro: Here our tour of Maiden's Castle comes to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
